title: Functorial flat resolutions of module objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category whose tensor
product is additive in each variable, and let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative monoid object.
In a monoidal abelian category, call an object $F$ *flat* if $F\otimes-$ and $-\otimes F$
are exact. A *functorial flat resolution* is a functor $P$ with flat values together with a
natural epimorphism $\pi_M\colon P(M)\to M$. Suppose $\mathcal C$ has a functorial flat
resolution. Then so does $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$, with the relative tensor product
of [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor]. It is given by the free modules
$\mathcal R\otimes P(M)$ and the maps
$$
\mathcal R\otimes P(M)\xrightarrow{\mathcal R\otimes\pi_M}\mathcal R\otimes M
\xrightarrow{\gamma_M}M .
$$

proof.text: Because $\mathcal C$ is closed, tensoring with any fixed object is a left adjoint and therefore preserves colimits; in particular $\mathcal R\otimes-$ preserves finite colimits. Thus [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] applies, and [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] supplies the symmetric monoidal structure on $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$.

Let $F$ be flat in $\mathcal C$. The coequalizer description of the relative tensor product ([def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]) and the associativity and unit isomorphisms give a natural isomorphism $(\mathcal R\otimes F)\otimes_{\mathcal R}M\cong F\otimes(\mathcal R\otimes_{\mathcal R}M)\cong F\otimes M$. Hence, after applying the forgetful functor, tensoring over $\mathcal R$ with the free module $\mathcal R\otimes F$ is the exact functor $F\otimes-$. The forgetful functor is faithful and preserves finite limits and colimits ([lem-sfb-modobj-forget-faithful], [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-left-exact], [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-right-exact]); the kernel and cokernel lemmas ([lem-sfb-modobj-kernels], [lem-sfb-modobj-cokernels]) identify these module-category limits and colimits with the underlying ones. It also reflects isomorphisms: if the underlying map of a module morphism is an isomorphism, its underlying inverse is module-linear by composing the module-linearity equation with that inverse. Hence exactness of the underlying sequence is equivalent to exactness in the module category. Therefore $(\mathcal R\otimes F)\otimes_{\mathcal R}-$ is exact, and symmetry from [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] gives exactness of $-\otimes_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal R\otimes F)$. Thus $\mathcal R\otimes F$ is flat.

For each $M$, define $q_M=\gamma_M\circ(\mathcal R\otimes\pi_M)$. The associativity law for the action makes $q_M$ $\mathcal R$-linear, and naturality of $\pi$ and of the action makes $q$ natural in $M$. Since $\mathcal C$ is closed, $\mathcal R\otimes-$ preserves colimits and hence sends the epimorphism $\pi_M$ to an epimorphism. The action map $\gamma_M$ is split epic with section $(\eta\otimes M)\lambda_M^{-1}$ by the unit law. Thus $q_M$ is a composite of epimorphisms, hence an epimorphism. By the preceding step, each source $\mathcal R\otimes P(M)$ is flat, so $q$ is the required functorial flat resolution.
